correctness.rationale: The real ℓ4 smooth norm gives x⊥B y iff Σx_i³y_i=0. Every unit Birkhoff pair is reduced, including both orientations, to r∈[0,1]. The two norm fourth-powers and all Taylor coefficients follow from direct binomial identities. J(r)^4=r(1-r)^4/(1-r+r²)^3 has a unique nondegenerate maximum at r0=2−√3, with J=c and S=1/√3. Uniform convergence excludes remote and reversed-sign maximizers; strict local concavity plus implicit function theory proves an analytic unique r_t for small t>0. Symbolic algebra confirms P(r0)/c=1−13√3/18 and −P′(r0)/J″(r0)=3√3−6. Standalone checker proves key algebraic identities symbolically and performs supplementary high-precision numerical tests; finite tests do not establish global quantifiers.

value.rationale: The newly introduced D_t^B has a natural need for a smooth non-Hilbert test case beyond its global inequalities. The two finite-skew coefficients identify nontrivial curvature effects absent from the limiting approximate-symmetry invariant, while uniqueness and zero first-order drift give precise structural information about extremizers. This is not a renamed established constant, arbitrary slice or mere numerical evaluation: it is an exact motivated singular-parameter benchmark, limited to real ℓ4².
